subject: research/mimic-anycontext-prompt
professional: an NLP researcher who works on machine-generated-text detection and prompt optimisation (a reviewer for ACL or EMNLP workshops), who would check that the evaluation splits are leak-free, that the AUROC numbers reproduce from the raw scores, whether selection effects are separated from noise, and whether the result is new relative to the zero-shot LLM detection literature

evidence.correctness: Ran python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 7 tests, OK. Recomputed independently with a separate numpy script (own AUROC via pairwise comparison, own selection loop, not importing anyprompt.py or core.py) from the shipped scores.json (512 keys, 10 or 30 scores each, as designed): plain 0.2775, universal held-out 0.29264, universal on seen families 0.30407, per-family 0.31056, oracle 0.33375, 1-AUROC flip 0.7074, recipes plain 0.08778, and all 16 candidate mean AUROCs (min 0.2710, max 0.3136) all match results.json and the README table to the printed digits. The README deltas (+0.015 universal, +0.033 per-family, spread about 0.04) recompute as 0.0151, 0.0331, 0.0426. Also reran the model itself: loaded Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from Hugging Face and rescored the first 8 test texts of recipes and reviews (human and llm) with candidate 0 through load()/single_user(): max absolute difference to the cached scores.json values was 0.0 on all four cells, so the cache is not fabricated and the pipeline is deterministic. Hanley-McNeil standard error for AUROC 0.3 with 30+30 texts is about 0.067, consistent with the README's 'roughly 0.06'. Not independently re-run: the other 500-odd cells (80 CPU-minutes) and the RAID labels themselves.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim. 7 tests: exist and pass. results.txt, results.json and figure.svg exist and agree with each other; figure.py runs and leaves the committed svg unchanged (git status clean). scores.json and candidates.json shipped, so the analysis step runs without a model. anyprompt.py main() is resumable and runs. Live-page and README Reproduce commands name files that exist. Stubs or TODOs: none. Declared non-goals (no imitator, no LLM proposer, one model, one seed) are stated and not claimed. Minor: no requirements file (pyenv.py is the install route), and the 'fairness by writer group' check is declared not run.
evidence.verification: Test command: 7 tests pass. Mutation 1: in regimes() changed the universal pick's training families from 'fams not in held' to all fams, i.e. a held-out-family leak, the central validity property of the study. All 7 tests still passed (fake data makes candidate 2 best everywhere, so leaking changes nothing; test_held_out_family_never_selects_the_prompt checks a set difference it recomputes inside the test, not the code under test). Mutation 2: changed the tie-break in pick() from -c to c (ties go to the last candidate, not plain, contradicting the README rule): all 7 passed, because test_ties_go_to_plain uses a single candidate. Both reverted with git checkout, tree clean. Tests only cover helper plumbing on synthetic data; none checks the AUROC numbers against the shipped scores.json or results.json, so a regression in analyse() would not be caught.
evidence.craft: Read anyprompt.py (about 130 lines), tests/test_anyprompt.py, mimic-loop/core.py (auroc, trunc) and mimic-loop/lm.py. Clean and short; the cache-then-select design is good (every regime shares the same model calls). Defects: the held-out leak guard test is vacuous (see verification); core.auroc is O(n*m) pure Python and returns nan on empty input without a guard downstream; the results.json write and the scores.json cache are not atomic (json.dump of the whole cache after each candidate, a kill mid-write corrupts it); load() asserts rather than raising a readable error; sys.path insertion plus a sibling-directory import couples this directory to mimic-loop; the 'lm' import is lazy by design. No type hints or linter. No unhandled-input path matters for a research script.
evidence.claims: Checked: every number in the README results table and bullets against results.json (all match, see correctness); 'no prompt reaches 0.5 on any family, best 0.424 reviews' matches the per-family oracle column (reviews 0.424); 'on recipes it is 0.09' matches 0.088; '0.934 for the n-gram detector' is in mimic-anycontext-detect/README.md; 'mimic-loop paired accuracy started at 12%' is loosely backed (the 0.12 start in mimic-loop's reddit rows), the README gives no row reference. Limits section is honest and thorough (one model, 16 prompts, SE about 0.06, one seed, non-adaptive text). The headline is correctly labelled negative and preliminary, and the 1-AUROC=0.71 aside is flagged as 'not tested as a method'. No marketing claims, no fake reviews, attribution to RAID and Qwen present, AI-assistance statement present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun the analysis from scores.json in seconds, swap in another model (the cache layout is documented, and mimic-anycontext-size already did this follow-up with 1.5B), and reuse the splits. But as a finding it is thin: no confidence intervals or bootstrap on the headline means (only a prose SE), 16 random fragment subsets is not a prompt search in the sense of APE, GrIPS or OPRO, no check that the sign inversion is not an artefact of the Yes/No framing, answer-token choice or chat template (a 'written by an AI model? Yes/No' control with flipped wording is the obvious ablation and was not run), one model, one seed. It supports 'this pipeline on this model does not work' rather than a general claim, which is exactly what the README says. Nearest prior work: zero-shot LLM detection of generated text, e.g. Bhattacharjee and Liu 2023 (Fighting fire with fire: can ChatGPT detect AI-generated text?), Dugan et al. 2024 (RAID, which this uses), and prompt-search methods (Zhou et al. 2022 APE, Prasad et al. 2023 GrIPS); the repository's own mimic-loop and mimic-anycontext-detect/-size are closer. Small instruction-tuned models doing worse than chance as zero-shot AI-text judges is a known pattern, so the result is a confirmation on this suite, not new; the held-out-families-for-prompts framing is the novel slice and the null result there is only weakly informative because there was nothing to transfer.
evidence.domain: Compared against detection-evaluation practice (RAID/MAGE style): AUROC on matched-length texts with a length control is right, disjoint selection and test splits are right, leave-two-families-out is a reasonable design, and reporting an oracle as optimistic is good. Departures a reviewer would flag: single seed and no resampling over the 10+10 selection texts or the candidate set, so the +0.015 universal-versus-plain gain has no interval (the README concedes it is within selection noise); text trimmed to 400 characters; machine text from three similar RAID chat generators with the plain prompt only; no calibration or threshold analysis (AUROC only, no TPR at fixed FPR, the metric detection papers report); the 'inversion' may reflect label-word priors of a 0.5B model rather than a detector property, untested. Method is sound for what it claims; not publishable as is.

defects.what: Held-out-family leak guard is untested: replacing the universal pick's training families with all families still passes all 7 tests; the 'never selects' test checks a set difference computed inside the test, not regimes()
Tie-break rule (ties go to the plain prompt) untested for more than one candidate: changing -c to c in pick() passes all tests
No test checks the analysis against the shipped scores.json/results.json, so a regression in analyse() or auroc would go unnoticed; headline means have no bootstrap interval
The inversion is not controlled against prompt-framing artefacts (no flipped 'Was this written by an AI?' wording control), so 'the detector is inverted' may be a Yes/No bias
The 12% mimic-loop figure is cited without a table or row reference
scores.json cache is rewritten whole after every candidate, not atomically

verdict: The numbers are real and the write-up is honest: all headline and per-family AUROCs, the 16 candidate means and the selection regimes recompute exactly from scores.json with an independent script, and a rescore of 32 texts through the actual Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct pipeline matched the cache to 0.0, so nothing is fabricated or unreproducible. The README states the right limits and labels the result negative and preliminary. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 2: two seeded mutations in core selection logic (a held-out-family leak, and the plain-wins tie rule) both survived all 7 tests, which only exercise helper plumbing on synthetic data. As research it is a faithful small confirmation that a tiny instruction model is a below-chance zero-shot AI-text judge, not a new result; it lacks intervals, seeds, a framing control and a threshold-level metric that a detection reviewer would ask for first. Small fixes: a test that runs regimes() on fake data where a leak would change the pick, a multi-candidate tie test, and a test pinning analyse() to results.json.
